sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Medical Device FDA 510(k) Filing and European CE Mark Compliance

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition, with modern European Union regulations and certain common-law influences in commercial practice)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (signed 13 May 1995)

Treaty between the United States of America and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (concluded 3 April 1996, as amended)
Convention on the Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (OECD / Council of Europe, as amended in 2010)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) – provisions on right of establishment and free movement of capital

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as consolidated and amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 February 2019 on the practical functioning of the RBE; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Circulars 19/732 and 20/758; FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 transposed into Luxembourg law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each partner and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the respective country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for non-EU/EEA documents); for EU/EEA documents, a notarised copy under Luxembourg law is sufficient

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence for each non-resident partner or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority of the partner's jurisdiction of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / extract from the commercial register (for corporate partners)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry in the corporate partner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, if issued by Luxembourg LBR, certified extract from the Luxembourg Business Registers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original notarised power of attorney for any legal agent acting for the SCSp during incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction where the document is executed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the POA is signed outside Luxembourg) or notarial certification in Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft notarial deed of formation of the SCSp (société en commandite spéciale) — including the articles/partnership deed and registered office declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarisation directly authorised by Luxembourg law; no apostille required if issued by Luxembourg notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, UBOs, and authorised signatories against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (CFSP), the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN), and any national Luxembourg list issued by the Financial Intelligence Unit (cellule de renseignement financier) or the Commissariat au Renseignement. Screening must occur at onboarding (pre-incorporation), at least daily during the business relationship, and upon any triggering event (e.g., change of ownership). Results must be documented in writing and retained for a minimum of five years. Screening tools must be CSSF-approved and provide audit trails. Additionally, enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies to any foreign PEP, family members, and close associates, including determination of source of wealth and source of funds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (LBR-RCS) – official online portal: https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in Latin script. The legal denotation and any descriptive element must be in French, German, or Luxembourgish. If a non-Latin-script name is desired, a mandatory Latin transliteration must be lodged with the registry, and the French or German translation must be incorporated into the partnership deed. The legal form suffix must appear as 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or 'SCSp'. The name must not be confused with an existing registered name or be overly generic.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant receives a written reasoned decision. The applicant may submit a written request for re-examination within 15 days of the rejection notice. If the re-examination is unsuccessful, a formal administrative appeal may be lodged with the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg (Tribunal Administratif) within one month of notification of the final refusal. A name reservation valid for 30 days may be extended once for an additional 15-day period upon payment of the applicable extension fee and submission of a renewed application, provided that the original name search remains valid and no conflicting registration has occurred.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional — a virtual office is acceptable for a non-trading professional consultancy (e.g., medical device regulatory consulting) provided that the service provider is a licensed domiciliation agent under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies. The agent must maintain a physical local address, accept official communications, make business records available on request, and comply with the UBO register disclosure requirements. A mere mail-forwarding address or drop-box arrangement without a locally registered domiciliation license is not permitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; currently estimated at 15–25% annual probability for a low-risk regulatory consultancy, driven primarily by LBR verification campaigns, CSSF anti-money-laundering desk audits, and occasional unannounced on-site checks by the tax administration (ACD) or the Social Security Inspectorate in the context of economic substance verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name reservation and clearance filing with Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of EUR 30 (converted at USD 1.00 = EUR 0.87) plus small online handling fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarised draft deed and notary verification services for SCSp formation (pre-inception drafting and registration preparation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff (tarif notarial); average market fee of EUR 2,000 for a standard SCSp deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of the chosen corporate name and object into French or German (if the original name is in a non-local language)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (approved by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-page rate, typically USD 30/page for 5 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalisation of foreign partner documentation (passport copies, tax residency certificates, certificate of good standing, corporate extracts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authority (Ministry of Foreign Affairs / State office) and Luxembourg consulate (if applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document governmental fee: USD 20–35 per apostille/legalisation; estimate for 4 documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Virtual office / registered office address (first year fee) with licensed domiciliation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: USD 100–150 per month for a low-risk professional entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC partner and UBO background screening — customer due diligence, sanctions, PEP, and adverse media checks
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance service provider / external legal advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for low-risk profile: USD 750–900, including initial screening and set-up of continuous monitoring

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner registration fee — submission to Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) via Chamber of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Chamber of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory handling fee of approximately EUR 65–75 (based on official tariff)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence review and custom entity structure opinion (pre-incorporation, UBO piercing, commercial substance assessment)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent law firm (advocat) or tax/legal advisory firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee or hourly rate; typical market band USD 1,500–2,500 for cross-border UBO policy review and structure memo

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 944-1 through 944-22 (SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA), as amended; Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited partnership agreement (Contrat de société / Statuts) executed by all partners, filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations - RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum paid-up capital for SCSp; capital contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement and may be in cash, in kind, or by industry. No escrow account or bank certification is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the capital commitments and subscription schedules of the Limited Partners are hereby approved and the corresponding capital accounts are credited; (2) that the registered office be established at [address], Luxembourg, and the General Partner is authorised to execute the office lease and related service agreements; (3) that [Name] be appointed Managing Partner (Gérant), with full powers to open bank accounts, sign correspondence, and represent the SCSp before the RCS, tax authorities, and third parties; (4) that the Managing Partner is instructed to file the partnership agreement with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, procure publication in the RESA, and complete all AML/KYC, UBO, and tax registrations; and (5) that this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability verification and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online name search portal and RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a prior name availability search in the RCS index to confirm the proposed corporate name is unique and not misleading; finalise and execute the SCSp limited partnership agreement (contrat de societe) in writing, either by private deed or notarial deed at the partners' election, including the corporate name, registered office address, corporate purpose (objet social) restricted to MedTech regulatory advisory services, capital commitments of each partner, profit-sharing ratio, identity and powers of the General Partner, and rules for transfer of partnership interests.
required_dossiers: Completed name availability search request
Draft SCSp limited partnership agreement
Valid passport or national ID of each partner and ultimate beneficial owner
Proof of residential or registered address of each partner
If the General Partner is a legal entity: extract of its register, certificate of good standing, and board resolution authorising signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for conflict or misleading character, amend the name and re-submit; any formal refusal by the RCS may be appealed to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within three months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the RCS and publication in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of signature, submit the electronic registration request through the LBR portal; upload the fully executed SCSp partnership agreement, the list of managing partners and authorised signatories with specimen signatures, the statement of the scope of representation powers, and the proof of registered office; the RCS then assigns the registration number by activating the file and publishes the statutory notice in the RESA.
required_dossiers: Signed SCSp partnership agreement
RCS registration form (declaration de depot)
List of managing partners (gérants) and authorised signatories with specimen signatures
Proof of registered office (lease deed or approved domiciliation agreement with a Luxembourg service provider)
Statement confirming authorised representation scope and joint signature rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a request for rectification (demande de regularisation), respond through the electronic platform within the prescribed deadline, typically 15 to 30 days; upon two unsuccessful submissions, the applicant may appeal the refusal to the Luxembourg District Court within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, social security, and beneficial owner registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Luxembourg Business Registers UBO register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After activation of the RCS file, apply to the ACD for corporate income tax and municipal business tax registration; as the SCSp invoices consulting services, register with the AED for Luxembourg VAT (TVA) using the appropriate form; if employees are hired, register as an employer with the CCSS; finally, file the beneficial ownership (UBO) declaration on the dedicated LBR portal, attaching the partnership agreement and identification documents of all ultimate beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extrait du registre)
SCSp partnership agreement
RCS company identification number confirmation
Identification of all managing partners and beneficial owners
Bank account details for tax payments and refunds
VAT registration form (formulaire 645) where applicable
Employer registration form (for CCSS, if hiring staff)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or queried, corrections can be filed directly with the relevant administration; late UBO filing carries criminal sanctions, so immediate remedial electronic filing is essential; tax penalties for late registration can be mitigated by voluntary disclosure and prompt settlement of any assessed interest.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and AML/KYC compliance procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Luxembourg credit institution (bank), subject to supervision of the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the authenticated RCS extract and partnership agreement to the selected Luxembourg bank, complete the KYC and source-of-funds questionnaires, and execute the account opening mandate in accordance with the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on AML/CFT; for a pass-through SCSp, the bank may request a tax opinion, a substance memo, and evidence of intended consulting contracts; the account is activated only after successful compliance screening of all partners and signatories.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate and registration number
SCSp partnership agreement and resolution conferring signatory powers
UBO declaration and identification of all partners
Certificate of good standing and constitutional documents of corporate general partner
Bank reference letters or prior account statements
Source-of-funds evidence and explanation of expected transaction flows
Projected activity overview and pro-forma invoices for the first 12 months
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests supplemental information, provide the requested substance documentation, tax opinion, or updated business plan; if the account opening is refused, apply to another Luxembourg credit institution or lodge a complaint with the CSSF; temporary payment solutions while awaiting account activation may be arranged through regulated payment institutions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the SCSp is engaged in unregulated international MedTech regulatory advisory services (ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541690) and does not operate any industrial plant; no operating license from the Ministry of the Economy or the Directorate-General for SMEs and Entrepreneurship is required at formation. Any expansion into regulated commercial premises would trigger assessment under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to trades and professions.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no manufacturing, commercial establishment, or industrial operating permit is required for the sole activity of FDA 510(k) filing and CE Mark compliance consulting; standard RCS registration and VAT/AED registration are the only administrative authorisations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the registered activity is office-based consultancy with no physical plant, no production line, no land disturbance, and no trigger thresholds under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; no preliminary EIA screening or full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - there are no wastewater discharge points, no VOC or combustion emissions, and no regulated industrial waste streams; the only obligations are the disposal of municipal office waste via the local commune collection system and compliance with the general waste management regulations of the Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable at formation - the SCSp will occupy a standard administrative office; the registered office lease must comply with the Luxembourg Building Regulations (Règlement des bâtisses) and the general fire safety requirements applicable to office premises. If the entity later hires employees, workplace clearances under the Labour Code (Code du travail), fire safety certification from the municipal fire service, and occupational health registration with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) will be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income and corporate taxation. Principal digital portal: MyGuichet.lu, with statutory company filing via the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL/RBE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident or foreign entity intending to perform taxable supplies in Luxembourg must submit a standard VAT registration application (Form 7 or equivalent) through MyGuichet.lu before commencing taxable activity. If the foreign entity is established outside the EU, it must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative (représentant responsable) jointly liable for VAT. The application must state the foreign corporate details, intended activity, and expected turnover. Upon successful registration, the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT number (TVA ID) without material delays; domestic direct tax registration may be triggered by permanent establishment presence or real estate ownership requiring separate ACD formalities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not employ a check-the-box regime. The SCSp is by default treated as fiscally transparent for Luxembourg corporate income and net wealth tax purposes; each partner is taxed on their allocable share of the partnership's income. There is no general statutory election to be treated as taxable, but treaty and domestic hybrid mismatch provisions under ATAD-compliant Luxembourg law (Law of 2 July 2019) may recharacterize certain opaque participations where income is disregarded by one jurisdiction. No form-based pass-through election is statutorily available; tax transparency is mandatory legal default.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-resident and foreign service suppliers: no turnover threshold; VAT registration is mandatory from the first euro of taxable supplies performed in Luxembourg. Resident small enterprises may apply the Luxembourg small-business exemption where annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) does not exceed EUR 35,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime. E-invoicing is permitted in B2B and mandatory for B2G public supply contracts, typically via PEPPOL. VAT returns and periodic EU sales lists must be filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu/E-file. There is no API-based pre-clearance of invoices; however, export evidence and substantiating customs entries must be electronically retained for audit purposes. Standard VAT reporting follows EU Directive rules with monthly or quarterly filing obligations depending on turnover and taxable activity.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to intra-Community supplies (EU exports) and to supplies of goods dispatched outside the EU upon satisfaction of statutory export conditions. Services to non-EU business customers are zero-rated where the place of supply is outside the EU, such as offshore consulting services received by a non-established business for use outside Luxembourg; cross-border B2B services benefiting from reverse charge are subject to standard VAT rules depending on recipient status. Eligibility requires the supplier to obtain and preserve documentary proof of departure, export, or foreign place of use within the time limits prescribed by Luxembourg VAT law.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / electronic customs lodgement via Luxembourg customs) confirming exit of goods from the EU.
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR transport document evidencing cross-border movement or delivery.
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire/payment proof identifying the foreign customer and consideration paid, where required to substantiate the foreign place of use or export transaction.
Commercial invoice containing the VAT zero-rated reference, export seller, export buyer consignee, and Incoterms.
Contract or service agreement describing the nature, place of performance, and non-EU beneficial recipient for zero-rated offshore consulting services.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Misclaimed export zero-rating or insufficient export documentation triggers reassessment by the AEDT. The tax authority may apply a 5-year limitation period (7 years in cases of fraud or wilful misrepresentation). Penalties include up to EUR 5,000 for reporting and documentary deficiencies, interest on unpaid VAT at the statutory rate, recovery of the unraised VAT, and joint and several liability for the Luxembourg VAT representative. Criminal sanctions, including imprisonment under Luxembourg tax and customs law, may apply for fraudulent export filings, false invoices, or money-laundering facilitation connected to false VAT refund claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting as the Luxembourg member of the Eurosystem and subordinate to the European Central Bank (ECB) for euro-area monetary policy, foreign-exchange operations and reserve management. Prudential supervision of credit institutions, payment institutions and electronic-money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign-exchange control agency; exchange controls are abolished under the EU free-movement-of-capital regime, and the BCL's residual statutory powers are confined to Eurosystem liquidity operations, emergency liquidity assistance, macroprudential policy, and balance-of-payments external statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is the legal tender and is fully convertible for residents and non-residents. Luxembourg applies complete current-account and capital-account liberalisation pursuant to Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and EU Regulation (EC) No 184/2005. No exchange licence, central-bank approval, conversion restriction or repatriation permit applies to profit remittances, distributions to foreign limited partners, or return of capital from a Luxembourg SCSp. The practical constraints are limited to: (i) the SCSp's tax-transparent and contract-based character, which obliges remitters and the receiving bank to classify inflows as 'equity/capital contribution' and not as trading revenue in order to preserve the tax treatment; (ii) CRS/FATCA self-certification and the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) declaration; (iii) BCL balance-of-payments statistical declarations for cross-border flows above materiality thresholds; and (iv) standard AML/CFT source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence. Distributions from an SCSp are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax because the partnership is fiscally transparent and has no independent tax personality; each partner is taxed in their own jurisdiction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None in law or in practice. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio and no requirement to repatriate or convert export proceeds or cross-border service revenue, including FDA 510(k) filing fees, CE-mark conformity-assessment fees and regulatory consulting fees. Export proceeds may be held indefinitely in EUR or in any foreign currency, in Luxembourg or abroad. The only compliance duties are: (i) BCL balance-of-payments reporting — the resident credit institution files on behalf of the SCSp for ordinary cross-border payments, but the SCSp itself is required to report directly where a single transaction reaches or exceeds EUR 12,500 or cumulative cross-border transactions reach or exceed EUR 125,000 over a rolling 12-month period; (ii) retention for at least five years of the underlying commercial documentation (engagement letters, invoices, FDA/CE submission dossiers, bank confirmations) to substantiate economic substance and true transactional purpose in an AML/CFT inspection; and (iii) verification that the exported services are not caught by sanctions or export-control restrictions applying to medical-device technical assistance where dual-use or embargoed end-users are involved.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE/Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility as a disbursement-only sub-rail; low feasibility as the primary treasury or capital-escrow rail. Under the Luxembourg PSD2 framework (Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, as amended) and CSSF supervision, an EU/EEA-licensed electronic-money institution or payment institution passporting into Luxembourg may be used for operating payments (vendor disbursements, small refunds, foreign-currency settlements). Wise Business, Airwallex, Revolut Business, Payoneer and similar offshore digital EMIs can be onboarded only if the SCSp provides its RCS/LBR registration extract, the notarised partnership agreement, the UBO declaration and a reference bank account at a Luxembourg credit institution. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI may not grant credit and must safeguard client funds in segregated accounts with an EU credit institution; (ii) the SCSp's lack of independent legal personality and its pass-through structure cause many EMIs to categorise it as a shell or regulated-vehicle risk, requiring a Luxembourg legal opinion; (iii) credit-card acquiring under the target payment rails must be routed through a licensed PSP such as Stripe or Adyen with a merchant agreement in the SCSp's registered name, clear MCC categorisation, and a documented transaction-flow and refund policy; card acquiring may not be used to collect funds for third parties, which would constitute an unlawful money-transmission or payment-service activity under the Luxembourg law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector (Article 23) and the PSD2 law. Recommended design: a primary operational and contribution account at BCEE or BIL, one EU-licensed EMI for small USD/EUR disbursements, and a Stripe/Adyen merchant settlement account feeding daily sweeps to the primary bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default expectation but not an absolute legal prohibition. For a non-resident SCSp whose general partner (associé gérant) and limited partners are foreign persons, the CSSF AML framework (CSSF Regulation 12-02; CSSF Circular 18/698, as amended by 20/744) requires the credit institution to positively identify the client, its authorised signatories and every ultimate beneficial owner. In practice, BCEE, BIL, BNP Paribas Luxembourg and Société Générale Luxembourg require at least one in-person interview with the general partner or with a duly mandated Luxembourg-resident agent holding a notarised power of attorney, a certified passport copy and a reliable secondary identity check, before account activation. Fully remote video onboarding is occasionally accepted only for low-risk structures with clean sanctions profiles, an existing banker introduction, and no cash-intensive or high-chargeback activity. The bank will also require a pre-account declaration in the Luxembourg RBE (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs) and an RCS commercial register extract. Recommended planning: a two-day Luxembourg visit for the general partner and, if practical, one limited partner; execution of the CSSF-compliant UBO forms before arrival; and retention of local counsel to co-ordinate the opening and to answer the bank's substance questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through contract-based structure: the SCSp has no independent legal personality, no minimum capital, and a foreign general partner; the bank may flag a shell, letterbox or substance-deficient vehicle used to obscure ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement (contrat de société) with capital-call provisions and capital-account mechanics; RCS/LBR registration extract; economic-substance dossier comprising a Luxembourg office lease or BPO agreement, a Luxembourg tax identification number, professional-indemnity insurance, salaries or management-fee evidence, and an organisational chart showing real management in Luxembourg; an economic-substance opinion from a Luxembourg tax advisor confirming bona fide activity under ISIC 7490 (medical-device regulatory consulting); template FDA/CE client engagement letters; and a written undertaking to retain underlying contracts and fee invoices for five years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border exposure to US, China and EU medical-device gateways: banks may perceive sanctions, export-control, or dual-use technology risk because the SCSp handles FDA 510(k) filings, EU MDR/IVDR notified-body procedures, and payments to overseas manufacturers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO identification package (passports, proof of address, source-of-wealth declarations) for each partner with their capital-account percentage; a commercial-rationale memorandum for each jurisdiction naming the FDA/US agent, the notified body (TÜV Rheinland, BSI, DEKRA, Intertek, GMED) and the manufacturer; pre-onboarding and quarterly denied-party-screening reports against OFAC, EU, UN and HMT lists; negative-media and sanctions-hit reports for all counterparties; written confirmation that no non-standard or embargoed medical device technology is being transferred; and a US-agent designation letter where FDA user fees are paid through a registered US agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contributions from third-country partners or affiliates, particularly where the remittance exceeds the EUR 12,500 / EUR 125,000 BCL reporting thresholds or is routed through an intermediary payment institution, creating a source-of-funds red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or accountant-verified financial statements of the contributing partner; six months of bank statements from the remitting account; signed capital-call notices cross-referenced to the SCSp business plan; SWIFT/SEPA messages with the purpose narrative 'Capital contribution to Luxembourg SCSp — equity injection, not consideration for services'; CRS/FATCA self-certifications for every limited partner; a source-of-wealth narrative for individual wires above EUR 500,000; and tax-clearance certificates confirming clean tax standing in the partner's country of residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Card-acquiring and online fee collection: the target payment rails include credit-card payments for professional regulatory services, which banks may perceive as chargeback, fraud, or unlicensed money-transmission exposure when attached to a tax-transparent partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed merchant agreement with a licensed PSP (Stripe, Adyen) describing the SCSp as the sole merchant, with dedicated transaction-flow diagrams, MCC codes, refund and chargeback policies; template FDA/CE client engagement letters and itemised fee schedules; monthly settlement reconciliation reports; a written undertaking that the SCSp does not accept funds on behalf of third parties and holds no client money; and a Luxembourg legal opinion confirming that the activities do not constitute reserved banking or payment services under the law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector (Article 23) or the PSD2 law of 10 November 2009.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions to the SCSp should be routed exclusively by wire from the partner's own bank account directly to the SCSp's designated contribution account at a Luxembourg tier-1 bank (BIL or BCEE). For EUR contributions, use a SEPA Credit Transfer where the payment is below the bank's internal large-value threshold, or a SWIFT MT103/MT202 for larger sums; for USD and other third-currency injections, always use SWIFT MT103 with the receiving field identifying the SCSp's IBAN and the beneficiary bank's SWIFT code. The payment message must carry a clear purpose narrative — 'Capital contribution to Luxembourg SCSp / direct investment — equity — not payment for goods or services' — and, where the bank's system requires an ISO 20022 ExternalPurpose code, use 'COMC' or 'CASH' as the closest accepted category while the narrative preserves the equity character. The SCSp must pre-deliver to the receiving bank: the executed partnership agreement, a capital-call notice signed by the general partner, an updated UBO/RBE declaration, and confirmation of the intended allocation to the partner's capital account. Because the SCSp has no statutory minimum capital, no regulatory escrow is required, but a segregated Capital Escrow Account is recommended as a voluntary ring-fencing measure to prevent commingling of contributions with operating revenue and to simplify the annual capital-account reconciliation. Inflows reaching or exceeding EUR 125,000 individually or cumulatively over 12 months will be reported by the bank to the BCL as direct investment equity; the SCSp must supply the remitter's name, country and relationship to avoid misclassification and preserve the pass-through tax treatment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements use three complementary clearing rails. First, SEPA Credit Transfer for all EUR payments inside the EEA — including notified-body fees (TÜV Rheinland, BSI, DEKRA, Intertek, GMED), European sub-consultants, laboratories and the general partner's management fees — with next-day execution and structured creditor references. Second, SWIFT MT103 for USD/EUR and third-currency cross-border wires to US agents, US FDA user-fee processors (effectively settled via the US agent's account or the Pay.gov card/ACH channel), and non-EEA suppliers; each MT103 must state the underlying invoice reference and the commercial purpose (regulatory consulting fee, conformity-assessment fee or procurement payment) to satisfy the beneficiary bank's due diligence. Third, documentary trade instruments for bulk procurement of medical-device components or finished devices from Asia or the USA: a confirmed irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued by SWIFT MT700 with Incoterms 2020 rules and a beneficiary-quality inspection certificate, and documentary collections on a documents-against-payment basis for smaller, repeatable procurements. Card-acquiring receipts from clients paying by credit card are settled by the PSP into a dedicated merchant settlement account and swept daily to the primary Luxembourg bank account; the merchant account is used only for collections and never for outbound trade disbursements. All disbursements must be supported by a standing treasury policy requiring two-signature authorisation (minimum EUR 10,000), a matching invoice in the SCSp's file, and an anti-typosquire check of the beneficiary IBAN before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Documented plain-vanilla deliverable EUR/USD FX forwards with a maximum tenor of 12 months, permitted only against identified commercial exposures (FDA filing fees, US agent fees, invoced USD receivables).
FX swaps (spot/forward combinations) for short-term conversion of USD card-settlement receipts into EUR without creating an open currency position.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to currencies without a deliverable onshore market accessible to a Luxembourg non-resident entity (for example CNY/CNH or INR) for payments to Asian notified bodies or device manufacturers.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for longer-dated procurement or fee commitments, subject to EMIR clearing thresholds and trade-repository reporting obligations administered by the hedging bank.

Zero-cost collar option strategies where the bank's derivatives-suitability assessment permits them; naked speculative positions are expressly prohibited under Luxembourg corporate-benefit doctrine, EMIR appropriateness rules, and the SCSp's partnership agreement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS annual confirmation (confirmation annuelle) of registered corporate data and beneficial owner file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month after the anniversary date of initial RCS registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in administrative monetary penalties of up to EUR 2,500; continued non-compliance can trigger RCS strike-off actions, loss of good standing, and inability to obtain official RCS extract certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts / financial statements deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels) if the SCSp is not covered by an exemption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the partners and no later than seven months after the balance sheet date; for calendar-year undertakings, the usual filing deadline is 31 July following the year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit annual accounts may lead to court-ordered publication of the omission, civil default fines of up to EUR 10,000, and ultimately judicial dissolution or strike-off upon repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership income tax return (déclaration fiscale annuelle / BOP 100) for the fiscally transparent SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg direct tax authority (Administration des contributions directes, ACD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year SCSp, the annual tax return is generally due by 31 December of the following tax year; a professional filing extension may apply when the return is prepared by an approved tax advisor.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subjects the SCSp to a late filing penalty of 10% of taxes due, monthly late interest at 0.7%, and administrative penalties; failure may also result in the loss of deductions and credits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SCSp is not automatically subject to statutory audit. A mandatory audit by an approved revealur d'entreprises agrée is required if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at balance sheet date: total balance sheet EUR 20,000,000; net turnover EUR 40,000,000; average workforce of 250 employees. Audit is also compulsory if the SCSp is a regulated UCITS/AIF under CSSF supervision or if the partnership agreement imposes a statutory auditor appointment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register and accounting; IFRS is permitted for consolidated accounts and for certain regulated undertakings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Luxembourg beneficial owners register (RBE) regime, there is no separate annual UBO filing. The SCSp must maintain current beneficial-owner data and file any update resulting from partnership-interest transfers or other changes within 30 days. During the annual RCS confirmation, the SCSp must confirm that the beneficial-owner information lodged with the RBE remains accurate; if no change has occurred, no additional UBO filing is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners / partnership-interest holders with capital accounts
Register of directors/managers (where natural or corporate managers are appointed)
Minute book of management/general partner decisions and UBO register maintained under the RBE law

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – USD 4,000 per annum for standard Luxembourg registered-office and corporate-agent services for an SCSp
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – USD 15,000 per audit engagement for a small or mid-size SCSp when an audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general corporate income tax holiday; SCSp is tax-transparent for Luxembourg CIT purposes unless it has elected to be taxable as a corporation; commercial companies may benefit from the 80% exemption on qualifying intellectual property income and a 30% flat-rate notional interest deduction on new equity capital.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Form 600 (Municipal Business Tax Return) filed via Luxembourg eCDF (Electronic Customs and Tax Declarations) portal; SCSp generally files only a nil/declarative return absent corporate election.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Standard filing deadline is 31 May of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; extensions may be granted until 31 December for group filings or complex cases.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification data: legal form, registration number (RCS), tax ID (TVA/RCS)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SCSp with non-resident partners must report the Luxembourg-taxable share allocable to resident partners; non-resident partners are not subject to Luxembourg CIT on their distributive share unless carrying on a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation: statutory book income adjusted for tax additions and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For SCSp, the pass-through allocation is reported on the partnership return; each partner’s share is computed in accordance with the partnership agreement and Luxembourg domestic allocation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and pre-payments (including withholding tax credits on dividends and interest)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may claim treaty relief or domestic withholding tax credits solely to the extent the income is effectively connected to a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax declaration (for corporate taxpayers; SCSp generally exempt)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SCSp is not subject to net wealth tax by default; non-resident partners remain outside Luxembourg net wealth tax scope.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty from EUR 250 up to EUR 2,500; daily penalty of EUR 25 per tax classification; late payment interest of 0.8% per month on outstanding corporate income tax; refusal to file may trigger an ex officio assessment plus a 10% increase of the tax assessed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (domestic law); 50% exemption applies for parent-subsidiary dividends when the parent is a fully taxable Luxembourg corporation holding at least 10% for 12 months; reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: File Luxembourg dividend withholding tax refund application on Form 270 (Declaration for refund of withholding tax) supporting the SCSp’s transparent status; the partner must provide a valid Luxembourg or foreign residence certificate and, for non-resident partners, the applicable double tax treaty relief certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty country. Carry out the refund request within the statutory limitation period, generally before the end of the year following the calendar year in which the dividend was paid.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg levies statutory withholding tax of 15% on dividends and, for payments to non-residents, a 15% withholding tax on interest paid by a Luxembourg professional debtor to non-resident lenders (subject to exemption for European Economic Area and treaty countries when the lender is the beneficial owner); royalty withholding tax under domestic law is 0% for outbound royalties, but treaty-protected royalty payments may be subject to a reduced rate of 5% or 0% under the OECD Model. Foreign withholding tax relief on inbound royalties is available under the participation exemption or through double tax treaties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 (local file threshold) and EUR 4,000,000 (master file threshold) based on group revenue and intercompany transaction value; full documentation required when the aggregate value of cross-border controlled transactions exceeds EUR 1,000,000 or when the group’s consolidated revenues exceed EUR 50,000,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies economic substance requirements based on EU case law (C-115/16, C-118/16 – Danish Cases), the ATAD general anti-abuse rule, and the OECD BEPS Action 6; an SCSp must demonstrate adequate staff, premises, and decision-making functions proportionate to its activities, particularly for intercompany financing and IP holding arrangements. The Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are not a separate domestic statute, but the Luxembourg tax authorities may challenge artificial arrangements under the abuse of law doctrine and the substance-over-form principle.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Luxembourg General Tax Law, Art. 59 LAL)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly submitting incomplete or false tax returns, concealing income derived from FDA/CE regulatory consulting services, or omitting a taxable permanent establishment in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and a fine of EUR 5,000 to EUR 100,000, or one of these penalties; additional civil penalties include 100% of the evaded tax and interest of 0.8% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for taxes withheld or collected but not remitted; criminal liability extends to de facto managers; civil restitution plus travel bans and a ban from managing commercial activities can be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox entity without real economic substance, serving solely to obtain treaty benefits or tax-transparent pass-through without commercial justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterisation of the structure (taxable corporate deemed entity), and administrative fine of up to EUR 250,000; back assessments with double interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in the artificial arrangement face personal fines up to EUR 50,000; in flagrant cases, criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion and an order for restitution of all tax savings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence or reporting suspicious transactions tied to the professional consulting revenue streams, or structuring fee payments to evade reporting thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; criminal sanctions up to 5 years imprisonment for directors or compliance officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML breaches; courts may impose a ban on holding directorship roles for up to 10 years, travel restrictions pending investigation, and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and submit the Luxembourg Local File or Master File upon request, or materially inaccurate arm’s length documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Documentation penalty of EUR 5,000 to EUR 25,000 per missing file, plus a 10% surcharge on the additional tax assessment resulting from the transfer pricing adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are liable for administrative fines; deliberate falsification of documentation may trigger criminal fraud penalties and a personal monetary liability equal to the tax shortfall.
